description: How the bot should react to the mobs it meets on its first nights, for threatOf and nightThreats. Hand-written; each entry names its evidence. confidence: 'documented' = docs/research/rotn-progression.md section 2 (hazard table), which cites the RotN wiki ([W-...]); 'vanilla' = Minecraft 1.12 behaviour that the RotN sources do not mention, unverified on this pack; 'verified' = read from the mod's bytecode in the pinned pack (javap -c -p (reads class files; runs no mod code) on the jar from the pinned server pack zip (SHA-256 90642fd5...f5205); SRG names checked against MCP stable-39-1.12 fields.csv), each entry citing the jar, class and methods; 'inferred' = not checked against the mod's code (each such entry says so in its evidence). Order (first match wins): a dangerous mob (entity-overrides.json) is always 'avoid' (source 'override'); then an entry in 'entities'; then the first 'classRules' entry whose pattern matches the dumped class's simple name (source 'inferred'); then a default from the threat level (entity(): hostile = IMob or bytecode-cited player targeting): hostile -> fight, otherwise ignore (source 'default'). Class rules apply to hostile mobs only. Reactions: 'fight' (fight, ideally at a choke point; retreat when outnumbered), 'keep-distance' (back off at once, do not melee), 'take-cover' (ranged attacker: stay behind cover), 'avoid' (do not engage; move away), 'ignore-unless-provoked' (neutral until attacked or provoked), 'ignore'.

general.summary: At night stay sealed in a cobblestone or stone shelter with light only inside; a dirt shack is not safe because mobs dig and pillar. Retreat if two or more hostiles come at once.
evidence: docs/research/rotn-progression.md section 2 (Mobs break in, Light attracts mobs, Zombies): [W-Tips], [W-Getting_Started], [HB survival/shelter/shelter_early]

minecraft:zombie.summary: Can carry pickaxes or axes, place weak scaffolding, break blocks and inflict hunger. Fight at a choke point with a shield, or stay sealed in. After killing one that carried a Parasite, move away. Retreat if two or more come at once.
evidence: docs/research/rotn-progression.md section 2, Zombies: [W-Zombie], [W-Getting_Started]

minecraft:skeleton.summary: Erratic movement and better aim than vanilla. Stay behind cover; do not strafe in open ground.
evidence: docs/research/rotn-progression.md section 2, Skeletons: [W-Getting_Started]

minecraft:spider.summary: Faster than vanilla, inflicts slowness, and other mobs ride it. Kill the spider first; avoid open ground.
evidence: docs/research/rotn-progression.md section 2, Spiders: [W-Getting_Started]

minecraft:creeper.summary: Hisses and stands still next to you, then explodes. Back off at once. Do not fight near stored items or wooden walls.
evidence: docs/research/rotn-progression.md section 2, Creepers and Fire Creepers: [W-Getting_Started], [W-Tips], [W-Progression_Stages]

specialmobs:firecreeper.summary: A Fire Creeper: explodes like a creeper and can burn dropped items. Back off at once; do not fight near stored items or wooden walls.
evidence: docs/research/rotn-progression.md section 2, Creepers and Fire Creepers: [W-Tips] 'Fire Creepers explode and can burn dropped items', [W-Progression_Stages]; the dump's specialmobs:firecreeper has the display name 'Fire Creeper'

minecraft:witch.summary: Throws harmful splash potions from range and drinks healing potions. Stay behind cover; do not stand in the open near it.
evidence: Minecraft 1.12 EntityWitch behaviour (ranged potion attack); not in the RotN sources, unverified on this pack. #111 follow-up (lead)

minecraft:illusion_illager.summary: Shoots arrows, makes illusion copies of itself and casts blindness. Stay behind cover.
evidence: Minecraft 1.12 EntityIllusionIllager behaviour (bow, illusions, blindness); not in the RotN sources, unverified on this pack. #111 follow-up (lead)

iceandfire:dread_lich.summary: A ranged caster: it always spawns holding a lich staff, so it fights from range, shooting skulls and summoning up to 5 minions. 50 health, armor 2. Stay behind cover; deal with the minions first.
evidence: IceAndFireRotN-1.9.1-1.2.1.jar: EntityDreadLich implements IRangedAttackMob; setEquipmentBasedOnDifficulty (func_180481_a) always puts IafItemRegistry.lich_staff in the main hand; setCombatTask adds the ranged DreadLichAIStrife (aiArrowAttack) when the main-hand item is lich_staff, else melee; attackEntityWithRangedAttack (func_82196_d) creates an EntityDreadLichSkull and, while getMinionCount() < 5, spawns getRandomNewMinion() and increments the count; applyEntityAttributes (func_110147_ax): max health 50, armor 2

iceandfire:if_troll.summary: A heavy melee hitter: 18 attack and 200 health on this pack (Ice and Fire's defaults are 10 and 50), armor 9. Do not fight it on the first night; stay sealed in. It flees the sun.
evidence: IceAndFireRotN-1.9.1-1.2.1.jar: EntityTroll extends EntityMob; initEntityAI adds EntityAIAttackMelee and TrollAIFleeSun; applyEntityAttributes sets attack damage from IceAndFireConfig.trollAttackStrength, max health from trollMaxHealth, armor 9
the pinned pack's config/ice_and_fire.cfg lines 491-495: S:"Troll Attack Strength"=18.0, S:"Troll Max Health"=200.0

minecraft:enderman.summary: Neutral until you look at its head or hit it. Do not look at it; do not attack it on the first night.
evidence: Minecraft 1.12 EntityEnderman behaviour (the dump marks it IMob, so entity() calls it hostile); not in the RotN sources, unverified on this pack

quark:ashen.summary: A skeleton whose arrows blind (Blindness, 2.5 s). Stay behind cover.
evidence: QuarkRotN-r1.6-190.jar: EntityAshen extends EntitySkeleton (vanilla bow AI); setEquipmentBasedOnDifficulty (func_180481_a) puts a tipped arrow (Items.TIPPED_ARROW, field_185167_i) of Blindness (MobEffects field_76440_q, 50 ticks) in its off hand, which a skeleton shoots

quark:dweller.summary: A zombie that is invisible from spawn until it attacks or takes damage; armor 3. Fight it like a zombie.
evidence: QuarkRotN-r1.6-190.jar: EntityDweller extends EntityZombie; onInitialSpawn (func_180482_a) adds Invisibility (MobEffects field_76441_p) for 2147483647 ticks; attackEntityFrom (func_70097_a, damage > 0) and attackEntityAsMob (func_70652_k) remove it; applyEntityAttributes: armor 3

iceologer:iceologer.summary: A spellcaster illager that summons ice blocks which fall on its target. 24 health. Stay under a roof or behind cover.
evidence: Frozen-Fiend-1.5.3.jar (the mod that registers iceologer:iceologer): EntityIceologer extends EntitySpellcasterIllager; its AISummonIceBlock creates an EntityIceCube; applyEntityAttributes: max health 24

mowziesmobs:naga.summary: A flying ranged attacker that circles its target. 30 health, 4 attack. Stay behind cover.
evidence: mowziesmobs-1.5.8.jar: EntityNaga implements IRangedAttackMob; initEntityAI adds AIFlyAroundTarget and AIRandomFly; applyEntityAttributes: max health 30, attack 4, follow range 45

rats:illager_piper.summary: Its ranged attack summons rats instead of shooting. Kill the piper first.
evidence: rats-3.2.21-1.12.2.jar: EntityIllagerPiper extends AbstractIllager implements IRangedAttackMob; attackEntityWithRangedAttack (func_82196_d) calls summonRat(); initEntityAI adds PiperAIStrife and EntityAIAttackMelee

ancientbeasts:bonepile.summary: A ranged attacker that strafes. 32 health. It shelters from the sun. Stay behind cover.
evidence: ancientbeasts-1.9.99999.jar: EntityBonepile extends EntityMob implements IRangedAttackMob; initEntityAI adds EntityAIAttackRangedStrafe, EntityAIRestrictSun and EntityAIFleeSun; applyEntityAttributes: max health 32

ancientbeasts:boulderer.summary: A zombie that climbs walls and leaps up ladders, so a low wall does not stop it. It also uses Speed and Invisibility effects.
evidence: ancientbeasts-1.9.99999.jar: EntityBoulderer extends EntityZombie; uses PathNavigateClimber and EntityAILeapLadder; references Speed (field_76424_c) and Invisibility (field_76441_p) potion effects (when they apply was not traced)

ancientbeasts:damcell.summary: A ranged attacker. 40 health. Stay behind cover.
evidence: ancientbeasts-1.9.99999.jar: EntityDamcell extends EntityMob implements IRangedAttackMob; initEntityAI adds EntityAIAttackRanged; applyEntityAttributes: max health 40

ancientbeasts:rifted_enderman.summary: Like an enderman: it targets a player who looks at it, then teleports and hits for 6. 40 health. Do not look at it.
evidence: ancientbeasts-1.9.99999.jar: EntityRiftedEnderman; its AIFindPlayer calls shouldAttackPlayer(EntityPlayer) (the enderman's stare check) and teleportRandomly(); initEntityAI adds EntityAIAttackMelee, AITakeBlock and AIPlaceBlock; applyEntityAttributes: max health 40, attack 6

ancientbeasts:frost_walker.summary: Casts ice magic (ice crystals) from range and also fights in melee. 32 health, 4 attack, armor 2. Stay behind cover.
evidence: ancientbeasts-1.9.99999.jar: EntityFrostWalker extends EntityMob; initEntityAI adds EntityAICastIceMagic (creates EntityIceCrystal), AIFrostWalkerSlowMelee and AIFrostWalkerFastMelee; applyEntityAttributes: max health 32, attack 4, armor 2

ancientbeasts:ghost.summary: A flying mob with 12 health. Its possession spell buffs the mob it targets (Absorption, Speed, Strength); on a player not in creative mode it applies the mod's Possessed effect for 20 s and deals 4 damage. Fight it.
evidence: ancientbeasts-1.9.99999.jar: EntityGhost extends EntityMob; PathNavigateFlying; initEntityAI adds EntityAIPossession. Its useMagic: if the target is an EntityLiving and not a villager, EntityLiving.func_70690_d adds Absorption (field_76444_x), Speed (field_76424_c) and Strength (field_76420_g) to it; if the target is a player not in creative mode (PlayerCapabilities.isCreativeMode, field_75098_d) or a villager, it adds ModPotions.POSSESSED for 400 ticks and deals DamageSource.causeMobDamage 4.0 x AncientBeastsConfig.GlobalDamageMultiplier. Possessed is handled in ModEvents.oooSpuki (a LivingUpdateEvent handler), not traced further; applyEntityAttributes: max health 12
the pinned pack's config/ancientbeasts.cfg line 50: D:"Global Damage Multiplier"=1.0

ancientbeasts:giant_zombie.summary: A giant: 180 health, 15 attack, armor 4, knockback resistance 4. Do not fight it; stay sealed in.
evidence: ancientbeasts-1.9.99999.jar: EntityGiant extends EntityMob; initEntityAI adds EntityAIGiantMelee; applyEntityAttributes: max health 180, attack 15, armor 4, knockback resistance 4

ancientbeasts:nekros.summary: A flying caster that summons a zombie and a skeleton and steals life. Only 12 health: kill it first.
evidence: ancientbeasts-1.9.99999.jar: EntityNekros extends EntityMob; UseDarkMagic creates an EntityZombie and an EntitySkeleton; LifeStealing damages its target (DamageSource.causeMobDamage) and heals itself (func_70691_i); applyEntityAttributes: max health 12

ancientbeasts:zealot.summary: A spellcaster illager: its weakening spell gives Slowness and Weakness, its buff spell helps allies. 24 health. It flees the sun.
evidence: ancientbeasts-1.9.99999.jar: EntityZealot extends EntitySpellcasterIllager; AIWeakeningSpell applies Slowness (field_76421_d) and Weakness (field_76437_t); AIBuffSpell creates an EntityBeam; initEntityAI adds EntityAIFleeSun; applyEntityAttributes: max health 24

ancientbeasts:sandy.summary: A tameable beast with two ranged attacks (sand spit and a tornado) and melee: 80 health, 6 attack, armor 4. It targets players only while untamed. Do not fight it on the first night.
evidence: ancientbeasts-1.9.99999.jar: EntitySandy extends EntityTameable; initEntityAI adds SummonSandShooter (creates EntitySandSpit), UseSandMagic (creates EntityTornado) and EntityAIMeleeConditional; its EntityAINearestAttackableTarget tasks target AbstractIllager, EntityVex and EntitySandy only, and it targets other living entities (players included) through two EntityAITargetNonTamed tasks, which run only while untamed (their predicate was not inspected); applyEntityAttributes: max health 80, attack 6, armor 4

minecraft:guardian.summary: Lives in ocean monuments and fires a laser beam. Stay out of the water near it and behind cover.
evidence: Minecraft 1.12 EntityGuardian behaviour (laser beam attack, ocean monuments); not in the RotN sources, unverified on this pack

minecraft:vindication_illager.summary: Swings an iron axe for heavy damage (13 on Normal in vanilla Java). Do not melee it on the first night; keep away or stay sealed in.
evidence: Minecraft 1.12 EntityVindicator behaviour (iron axe melee; Minecraft Wiki: 13 damage on Normal, Java Edition); not in the RotN sources, unverified on this pack

minecraft:slime.summary: Bounces and hits in melee; it splits into smaller slimes when killed (the smallest do no damage). Fight it, preferably not in a crowd.
evidence: Minecraft 1.12 EntitySlime behaviour (melee by size, splits on death, the smallest size deals no damage; spawns in swamps at night and in slime chunks below Y 40); not in the RotN sources, unverified on this pack

charm:spectre.summary: An underground ghost (spawns only at depth 24 or below, in darkness): 0.5 health and 0.01 attack, but on this pack its touch curses the player's armor or items. Kill it with one hit before it touches you; it disappears in light (level 8) and after 120 s.
evidence: Charm-1.12.2-1.4.1.jar: EntitySpectre extends EntityMob; initEntityAI adds EntityAINearestAttackableTarget(EntityPlayer) and EntityAIAttackMelee; applyEntityAttributes reads svenhjol.charm.world.feature.Spectre (defaults: max health 0.5, attack 0.01, speed 0.19); attackEntityAsMob (func_70652_k) curses items when Spectre.applyCurse, else applies Weakness; getCanSpawnHere (func_70601_bi) requires the bounding box at or below Spectre.spawnDepth; onUpdate (func_70071_h_) despawns it at Spectre.despawnLight; attackEntityFrom (func_70097_a) ignores fall (field_76379_h) and in-wall (field_76368_d) damage
the pinned pack's config/charm.cfg lines 832-846 and 858: B:"Apply curse"=true, I:"Despawn light level"=8, I:"Spawn depth"=24, I:"Spawn weight"=100, I:"Spectre lifetime"=120

classRules.summary: A creeper variant (Special Mobs, Primitive Mobs, NetherEx, Better With Mods): treat it as a creeper. Back off at once; do not melee it.
evidence: the dump: the class's simple name contains 'Creeper' (fathertoast.specialmobs.entity.creeper.*, net.daveyx0.primitivemobs.entity.monster.Entity*Creeper, ...); the creeper reaction is documented in docs/research/rotn-progression.md section 2
classRules.note: Inferred from the class name, not from each mod's code: a variant may not explode (Better With Mods' sheared creeper) or may explode differently (Primitive Mobs' rocket creeper). Keeping distance is the safe reaction either way.

classRules.summary: A skeleton variant (Special Mobs, Primitive Mobs, ...): treat it as a skeleton. Stay behind cover; do not strafe in open ground.
evidence: the dump: the class's simple name contains 'Skeleton' or 'Stray' (fathertoast.specialmobs.entity.skeleton.*, net.minecraft.entity.monster.EntityStray, ...); the skeleton reaction is documented in docs/research/rotn-progression.md section 2
classRules.note: Inferred from the class name: some variants fight in melee (brute, knight, ninja). Wither skeletons and their Special Mobs variants (Nether mobs, mostly melee) are excluded and get the default.

classRules.summary: A Special Mobs enderman variant: like an enderman, it targets a player who looks at it or hits it. Do not look at it; do not attack it on the first night. Some variants add effects (blindness, slowness, mining fatigue).
evidence: specialmobs-1.0.4_for_mc1.12.2.jar (from the pinned pack zip; javap -c -p, no mod code run): Entity_SpecialEnderman extends net.minecraft.entity.monster.EntityEnderman, and every variant (Blinding, Icy, Lightning, Mini, Mirage, Thief) extends Entity_SpecialEnderman; Entity_SpecialEnderman.initEntityAI (func_184651_r) calls EntityEnderman.func_184651_r (the vanilla stare-based targeting) and then initTypeAI; no variant overrides initEntityAI or adds a targeting task, and none refers to EntityPlayer
effects referenced: EntityBlindingEnderman Blindness and Night Vision; EntityIcyEnderman Slowness and Mining Fatigue (MCP stable-39 fields.csv names)
the vanilla enderman entry (minecraft:enderman) and Special Mobs' overworld chance 0.25 (the pinned pack's config/Special_Mobs.cfg, endermen _special_chance_exceptions dimension/overworld=0.25)
classRules.note: Matches classes whose simple name ends with 'Enderman'; entries win over class rules, so minecraft:enderman (vanilla) and ancientbeasts:rifted_enderman (verified) keep theirs. What each variant does when provoked was not traced.

classRules.summary: A Special Mobs witch variant: like a witch, it throws harmful potions from range. Stay behind cover. Some variants add effects (levitation, wither, blindness, poison).
evidence: specialmobs-1.0.4_for_mc1.12.2.jar (from the pinned pack zip; javap -c -p, no mod code run): Entity_SpecialWitch extends net.minecraft.entity.monster.EntityWitch, and every variant (Domination, Shadows, Undead, Wilds, Wind) extends Entity_SpecialWitch; Entity_SpecialWitch.initEntityAI calls EntityWitch.func_184651_r (the vanilla ranged potion attack) and then initTypeAI; no variant overrides initEntityAI or adds a targeting task

effects referenced: EntityDominationWitch Levitation and Weakness; EntityShadowsWitch Blindness, Night Vision and Wither; EntityWildsWitch and EntityUndeadWitch Speed, Fire Resistance, Water Breathing (and Poison for Wilds); Entity_SpecialWitch Slowness, Speed, Fire Resistance, Water Breathing, Poison and Weakness (MCP stable-39 fields.csv names)
the vanilla witch entry (minecraft:witch) and Special Mobs' overworld chance 0.25 (config/Special_Mobs.cfg, witches _special_chance_exceptions dimension/overworld=0.25)
classRules.note: Matches classes whose simple name ends with 'Witch', so Special Mobs' witch spiders (EntityWitchSpider, EntityWitchCaveSpider) are not caught. minecraft:witch keeps its own entry. Which potions each variant throws was not traced.
